The '''1979 FA Charity Shield''' was the 57th [[FA Community Shield|Charity Shield]], an annual English [[association football|football]] match played between the winners of the previous season's [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[FA Cup]]. It was held at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] on 11 August 1979. The match was contested by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], champions of the [[The Football League 1978-79|1978–79 Football League]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[1979 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[1978–79 FA Cup]]. Watched by a crowd of 92,800, Liverpool won the match 3–1.

This was Arsenal's tenth Charity Shield appearance and Liverpool's ninth. Arsenal made no changes to the first team which played in the FA Cup Final the previous season, whereas for Liverpool new signing [[Avi Cohen]] started on the bench. In the match Liverpool took the lead in the 38th minute when [[Terry McDermott]] scored past goalkeeper [[Pat Jennings]]. They extended their lead through [[Kenny Dalglish]] in the 63rd minute before McDermott added his second two minutes later. [[Alan Sunderland]] scored a consolation for Arsenal late on.

==Background and pre-match==
[[File:The old Wembley Stadium.jpg|thumb|[[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] was the venue for the Charity Shield.]]
The [[FA Charity Shield]] was founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> It was a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], and then by 1913 teams of amateur and professional players.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=The Times |location=London |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the Football League champions and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |work=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192421/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |url-status=dead }}</ref> This was the sixth year that [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] played host to the Shield.<ref>{{cite news|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |work=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] qualified for the 1979 FA Charity Shield as winners of the [[1978–79 Football League|previous season's]] First Division.<ref name="prev">{{cite news |title=The end of the beginning |first=David |last=Lacey |page=20 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=11 August 1979}}</ref> Under manager [[Bob Paisley]], the team amassed a then-record points total of 68 and conceded the fewest goals in a 42-game Football League season with 16.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool are Superchampions |first=John |last=Roberts |page=28 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=18 May 1979}} Liverpool's Football League points record has since been bettered, see:
*{{cite web |title=League Points |url=http://www.fl125.co.uk/records/league-points |publisher=Football League |access-date=26 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112223703/http://www.fl125.co.uk/records/league-points |archive-date=12 November 2017 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> The other Charity Shield place went to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] who beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] to win the [[1979 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[1978–79 FA Cup]].<ref name="prev"/> Arsenal led the game 2–0, but conceded twice late into the match before retaking the lead in the 89th minute; the final score was 3–2.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal at the last gasp |first=Hugh |last=McIlvanney |page=1 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=13 May 1979}}</ref> The game is referred to as the "Five-minute final" as three goals were scored in that time frame.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Five-minute final: Where are they now? |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/4525061.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2005 |access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref>

This was Arsenal's first appearance in the Charity Shield in 26 years; prior to the game they had won seven Shields ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]], [[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]] and [[1953 FA Charity Shield|1953]]), and lost two ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |title=England – List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |publisher=Rec. Sport. Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=2 April 2014 |first=James |last=Ross}}</ref> Liverpool had won three previous Shields outright ([[1966 FA Charity Shield|1966]], [[1974 FA Charity Shield|1974]], [[1976 FA Charity Shield|1976]]), shared two with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] ([[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]] and [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]]) and one apiece with [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] ([[1964 FA Charity Shield|1964]]). The club lost one Shield contest – against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in [[1971 FA Charity Shield|1971]]. Before the match Paisley told reporters, "Basically it is a conditioning game, part of the process of getting the players fit".<ref name="prev"/>

==Match==
Arsenal organised themselves similarly to their opponents and named an unchanged team from the one which won the FA Cup.<ref name="prev"/> Liverpool employed a traditional [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] formation, with [[David Johnson (footballer, born 1951)|David Johnson]] playing alongside [[Kenny Dalglish]] up front.  Defender [[Avi Cohen]] was named on the substitutes' bench, whereas [[Frank McGarvey]] – signed from [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the close season – was omitted from the matchday squad.

===Summary===
Liverpool dominated the opening exchanges, but struggled to create clear-cut chances. They almost went a goal behind when [[Frank Stapleton]]'s header forced goalkeeper [[Ray Clemence]] into action.<ref name="obre">{{cite news |title=The red gauntlet |first=Ronald |last=Atkin |page=32 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=12 August 1979}}</ref> Seven minutes before the interval, [[Terry McDermott]] scored for Liverpool. The midfielder collected a pass from [[Ray Kennedy]] who surged through the centre, turned left and from outside the penalty area struck the ball low into the bottom left-hand corner.<ref name="exre">{{cite news |title=Kings of Anfield make Arsenal suffer |first=James |last=Mossop |page=32 |newspaper=Sunday Express |location=London |date=12 August 1979}}</ref> Arsenal began the second half with more vigour, but struggled to suppress Liverpool's attacks. [[Alan Kennedy]] found space to shoot after a one-two with Ray, but his effort went over the post.<ref name="obre"/> Arsenal were forced to make a substitution around the hour mark after [[Sammy Nelson]] collided with McDermott and was concussed; [[Willie Young (footballer, born 1951)|Willie Young]] replaced him.<ref name="obre"/> Liverpool extended their lead minutes later. [[Alan Hansen]] intercepted an Arsenal attack, strode forward and passed the ball to Dalglish.<ref name="exre"/> The striker approached the penalty area, cut inside [[Steve Walford]] and curled the ball into the right-hand corner.<ref name="exre"/> [[John Hollins]] came on for [[David Price (footballer, born 1955)|David Price]], at which point Liverpool scored their third. Dalglish dispossessed [[Liam Brady]], but tripped himself in the process.<ref>{{cite news |title=Some Liverpool home truths |first=David |last=Lacey |page=22 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=13 August 1979}}</ref> Johnson collected the ball and played it back to Dalglish, who charged forward and sprayed a pass towards McDermott, the furthest forward player on the right. The midfielder's shot went under the legs of [[Pat Jennings]] and into the goal.<ref name="obre"/> [[Alan Sunderland]] scored a late goal for Arsenal having combined well with Stapleton. This did not dampen the spirits of the Liverpool spectators, who chanted, "What's it like to be outclassed?" and, "Why are we so great?" during the course of the 90 minutes.<ref name="obre"/><ref name="exre"/>

==Post-match==
Liverpool's performance was greeted with applause from both sets of supporters as [[Phil Thompson]] led his team up to the Royal Box to receive the Charity Shield.<ref name="exre"/> Paisley was delighted with the manner of his team's win and quipped, "I am just sorry we didn't get two points for it!"<ref name="exre"/> He praised the Wembley surface and said of McDermott's first goal "[It] captured what we are looking for – the run, the control and the finish were perfect."<ref name="exre"/> Arsenal manager [[Terry Neill]] described the match as a "great advertisement for football" and felt his side contributed greatly in periods. Of his opponents, he said: "Liverpool are a smashing side and I don't expect to meet anyone better this season."<ref name="exre"/> Indeed, Liverpool went on to retain the First Division title, withstanding pressure from Manchester United and ending their league campaign on 60 points.<ref>{{cite news |title=Understudies make Liverpool stars |first=Norman |last=Fox |page=12 |newspaper=The Times |location=London |date=5 May 1980}}</ref><ref name="tar">{{cite news |title=Weekend tables and results |page=12 |newspaper=The Times |location=London |date=5 May 1980}}</ref> Arsenal finished three places behind in fourth, and reached the finals of the [[FA Cup]] and [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], only to end the season empty-handed.<ref name="tar"/><ref>{{cite web |title=125 years of Arsenal history – 1976–1980 |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/125-years-of-arsenal-history-1976-1980 |work=Arsenal.com |date=1 October 2012 |access-date=27 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305152132/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/125-years-of-arsenal-history-1976-1980 |archive-date=5 March 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>
